relationships.subject: chronic sleep disruption
relationships.evidence_quote: N-arachidonoyl dopamine (NADA) levels were decreased in the TRN in the CSD group compared with the control group

relationships.subject: N-arachidonoyl dopamine
relationships.evidence_quote: NADA is an endocannabinoid that acts as an agonist for both cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1 receptor) and transient receptor potential V1 (TRPV1)

relationships.subject: thalamic reticular nucleus
relationships.evidence_quote: DREADDs-mediated activation of the TRN was accompanied by a decrease in neural dynamics in the VP

relationships.subject: N-arachidonoyl dopamine
relationships.evidence_quote: These results suggest that exogenous supplementation of NADA to the TRN could attenuate CSD-induced hyperalgesia.

key_findings: Chronic sleep disruption reduces TRN activity and NADA, decreasing TRN CB1 receptor activity, and disinhibiting VP to produce hyperalgesia.
NADA delivered to the TRN attenuates CSD-induced hyperalgesia via CB1 receptors.
